item.title: Making holograms with a pen plotter
item.description:
📝 On the right side I’ve drawn a schematic of what’s happening: the light finds a path from the light source to your eye that bounces off somewhere along the ridges left by your fingerprint. In other words, our reflective ridges have a highlight glare that moves at a speed that is inversely proportional to the radius of curvature of the ridge — just like how objects in the real world appear to move slower when they’re further away. To put this into practice, we will “render” a scene such that each point becomes a reflective ridge with a radius of curvature that is inversely proportional to the distance of the point from the camera.
🔗 Read more: https://blog.jordan.matelsky.com/Penplotter-holography/
